 WUCL Fantasy Matchday 5: Team reveal 
 November 17 
 0 comments
 17 November 2026 
 0 comments
 FPLReactions 
 Share:
 With the UEFA Women’s Champions League returning for Matchday 5, our WUCL Fantasy expert Joe shares his latest team, transfer plans and the players he’s backing ahead of the deadline.
 READ MORE: ­­­McGinn v Manzambi: How do the two Villa midfielders compare? 
 READ MORE: The best value FPL players of 2026/27 so far 
 It’s a quick turnaround in UWCL Fantasy, with Matchday 5 starting just six days after Matchday 4 ended. Last week’s 91 points pushed me into the top 50 overall, a rank I’m very pleased with at this stage.
 With two matchdays remaining, here’s how I’m currently lining up.
 TEAM REVEAL
 Neither goalkeeper kept a clean sheet last week, leaving me with just two points from the position. Despite that, I’m still happy with my rotation. Both face Pot 2 opponents on different days this week, followed by Pot 3 opposition in Matchday 6.
 Femke Pauels also averages more than six saves per Champions League game this season, so she can still rack up points without a clean sheet.
 DEFENDERS
 With Kadeisha Buchanan on the bench, I brought in Ellie Carpenter last week. My faith in Chelsea’s defence paid off, as the Blues made it four clean sheets from four Champions League matches.
 We won’t know Chelsea’s starting XI before the deadline this week, but I’m happy to keep Carpenter and Veerle Buurman for what looks like a must-win game against Paris Saint-Germain. Buurman has recorded at least nine ball recoveries in all four Champions League matches, making her excellent value. If either player misses out, Wednesday’s fixture gives me the chance to replace them with my Thursday options.
 Kim Everaerts was the big surprise last week, making 15 ball recoveries on her way to seven points. She nearly managed an even bigger haul, with OH Leuven holding onto their clean sheet until the 82nd minute.
 I could sell her this week, but there’s still plenty to like. Her Wednesday fixture gives me flexibility, while the potential for another big ball-recovery score makes her useful, even away to Juventus.
 Wendie Renard has now produced back-to-back 11-point hauls since returning to OL Lyonnes’ starting XI after injury. We also got further confirmation of her penalty duties. She stepped up for a late spot-kick, missed it, then thankfully converted the rebound.
 Only Lyon and Chelsea have kept clean sheets in all four Champions League matches this season. With defensive returns, ball recoveries and attacking threat all on offer, Renard is a lock in my squad.
 Selma Bacha is a more difficult decision. She’s a perfectly good hold given Lyon’s defensive form, but Arsenal away could be an opportunity to make a change.
 Real Madrid’s Bella Andersson (5.0m) is one alternative I’m considering. She plays on Wednesday, which would give me more flexibility, and I already have Renard covering Lyon’s defence. It’s something I’ll think over, particularly if I have a spare transfer.
 MIDFIELDERS
 Sandy Baltimore is someone I’m likely to sell this week. Chelsea’s attack has struggled in Europe, and we won’t get confirmation of her starting place before the deadline.
 Real Madrid’s Linda Caicedo (8.5m) looks a strong replacement. She’s scored or assisted in each of the last three matchdays, and we’ll know whether she starts before the deadline.
 Aoba Fujino was a fantastic addition last week, scoring twice for a 12-point return despite coming off at half-time. At 5.0m, with two favourable fixtures remaining, she looks excellent value for the rest of the league phase. However, if she starts on the bench, I may switch to Mary Fowler (5.0m) or Arianna Caruso (5.0m).
 Caroline Graham Hansen scored 10 points in Matchday 4, but that barely reflects how dominant she was. The Norway international created 11 chances, including four big chances, and had 15 touches in the opposition box. She could easily have finished with a 20-point haul.
 She’s currently flagged in Fantasy and remains a slight doubt after missing Barcelona’s game on Sunday. The club described her absence as a rest, though, so I’m hopeful she’ll be available on Thursday. If she makes the squad, she’ll likely be my Thursday captain.
 Clàudia Pina blanked for the first time this season against Arsenal, but she’s an easy hold. Servette have conceded 16 goals in the Champions League, more than any other side. Barcelona also rotated heavily in Liga F at the weekend, so I’m expecting a strong starting XI for this fixture.
 Klara Bühl continued her magnificent start to the season with a goal and Player of the Match award against PSG. She’s now scored or assisted in seven consecutive matches for Bayern Munich. Next up is Austria Wien, who will be without their first-choice goalkeeper through suspension.
 FORWARDS
 Khadija Shaw saw her run of scoring in seven consecutive games end at the weekend, as Manchester City lost 1-0 to Chelsea in a huge match in the title race. Her unexpected benching against Inter last week was frustrating, but I’m hoping she’ll start this time.
 Luckily, we’ll have City’s team news before the deadline. If Shaw misses out again, I could switch to someone like Real Madrid’s Felicia Schröder (7.6m). If she starts, she’ll likely be my captain.
 Ewa Pajor joined Pina in blanking for the first time this season against Arsenal, but I have no intention of selling her. As with her Barcelona teammates, I’m hoping for a strong lineup this week. It’d be silly to consider removing a forward of Pajor’s quality ahead of a match against the competition’s weakest defence.
 If Graham Hansen doesn’t make the squad, Pajor could take my Thursday captaincy.
 Melchie Dumornay finally returned to the points last matchday. Her goal proved enough to secure Player of the Match, giving her a welcome haul.
 Arsenal away is Lyon’s toughest remaining fixture, but Dumornay has an excellent record against the Gunners. She’s scored four goals and provided one assist in four meetings during her time in France. I’m happy to keep her this week, especially at her price.
 Best of luck for Matchday 5, everybody!
